reply.text:
Mostly yes. Ordinary tiredness from a long week or a rough night is a normal reason to train, just smarter: keep the session shorter, drop a set or two, and leave more reps in the tank than usual. Often you feel better ten minutes into the warm-up than you expected to.

The line I'd draw is between tired and run down. If you've been dragging for days, sleeping badly, and your lifts are sliding, that's a sign to take an easier day or a full rest day, not to grind through. Don't chase a PR on a day like that either.

If you tell me how tired you are today, I can set up a lighter session for you.
